correctness.rationale: For the complete parameter square, positive weights approach one with summable deviations. Their strict monotonicity gives exact maximal k-step weights for N>D and exact minimal moduli for N<D. Similarity estimates for each power give global lower bounds applying to all invertible intertwiners, attained by the bounded diagonal partial-product intertwiner; N=D is trivial. Integrable-derivative Euler–Maclaurin plus the elementary Li2 integral yields the two-term singular limit. The double-scaling estimate follows from a uniform Taylor remainder and a Riemann-sum limit. A standalone rational checker verified 7,350 exact finite k-block comparisons and 12 numerical asymptotic diagnostics; unrestricted proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Primary GRWS paper defines the weights and proves qualitative moment and subnormality classifications; the 2022 Hou–Ji–Xu introduction reproduces Shields’s equivalence between similarity and bounded contiguous product ratios. Neither statement identifies the infimum of ||X|| ||X^{-1}|| across all intertwiners or the q-Pochhammer and dilogarithmic singular/crossover profile. Actual published-finding corpus semantic searches for the exact invariant and aliases returned no covering result; closest shift entries concern power profiles, perturbative numerical radius, or periodic shift spectral radii. The full texts and source-specific materials inspected supply no stronger prior implication. An earlier equivalent diagonal-similarity minimax formula remains possible, and independent review is needed.
residual_risks: Earlier work on optimal diagonal conjugacy or similarity constants might imply the sharp infimum without spelling out q-geometric parameters.
Full text of the related GRWS quotient paper arXiv:2312.06390 and classical Clark–Misra 1985 was not examined; these are identified access limitations, not certified noncoverage.
A different series or dilogarithm parametrization may reproduce the singular law.

value.rationale: The benchmark family has rich and contrasting moment/hyponormal behaviors, making stability of its similarity to a canonical shift a natural operator-theoretic invariant rather than an arbitrary arithmetic evaluation. Sharp least conditioning (not merely similarity existence) separates contractive operators indistinguishable by their power norms from the model shift, quantifies exponential instability near geometric ratio one, and exhibits a critical coalescence scale with nontrivial finite limit. The three regimes supply useful normalization and conditioning thresholds for studying the same geometric shift families. The claim is bounded to one natural complete family, not suggested as a universal similarity formula.
